content:
maria: Heads up — after the scheduler tweak we pushed last night, multi-variant routes show a visible P99 regression (~12%). looks like small-batch fragmentation when variant-affinity is on. profiling attached in thread.
aj: ack. which signals point to fragmentation vs kernel mis-selection?
maria: main signals: 1) increased number of tiny batches (1-3 requests) for compat-mixed queues. 2) more kernel fallbacks on warmup (quant kernel -> reference) 3) KV-cache miss spikes during variant transitions.
cheng: can you paste the quick perf summary? numbers help.
maria: short dump:
```
route: /chat (mix A/B)
before: p50=32ms p95=78ms p99=128ms
after:  p50=34ms p95=85ms p99=144ms
batch size dist before: mode=8 mean=6
batch size dist after:  mode=5 mean=4.2
kv-hit rate before: 0.86 after: 0.71
kernel fallback count +42%
```
sam: yikes — KV hit drop is huge. that explains token cost and latency. did affinity setting reduce prefix coalescing?
aj: yes, affinity pins requests to variant buckets sooner which reduces compat merging. beneficial for per-variant caching but harms mixed traffic because we lose batching density.
cheng: so tradeoff: variant affinity -> better per-variant KV locality but worse cross-variant batching. we need a hybrid queuepolicy.
maria: tried quick experiment toggling token_budget from 120->200 (ms budget), allowed waiting longer to coalesce. p99 dropped ~5ms but p95 unchanged. cost increased slightly due to larger average batch.
aj: what about an adaptive budget: increase wait when compat-diversity high, shrink when compat-homogeneous? detect compat-entropy per window.
sam: also consider slight permissive compat merging: e.g., merge variants with same kernel profile and quantization rather than strict variant equality. would reduce kernel fallbacks.
maria: agreed. we saw kernel selection mismatch is a big factor: if combined batch contains variant with different quant params, runtime falls back to slower path. suggestion: group by kernel-compat set first, then by variant.
infra-bot: deploy:canary rebalanced-scheduler -> rolled back at 1951240050 by infra-bot (auto-rollback: p99>10% threshold)
aj: noted rollback. next steps I'd propose:
- implement a lightweight compat-hash that groups by (kernel_profile, quant_level, dtype) instead of variant id
- add entropy metric to scheduler to tune token_budget dynamically
- add KV-prefetch probe on variant-switch to warm cache for likely keys
cheng: add an A/B test route with gradual enable so we can measure cost delta per-100k reqs. also add trace sample for kernel fallback stack.
sam: I'll own the KV-prefetch probe. plan: prefetch top-5 prefix keys per user-session on variant-change, TTL 30s.
maria: I'll prototype compat-hash grouping and knob for token_budget adaptivity. will post back with simple perf snapshot.
aj: thanks. for triage can we annotate recent traces where kernel_fallback==true? need callsite and batch composition.
cheng: will add a filter in profiler to export those traces. expected to have small payloads (safe to collect).
maria: timeline: prototype by EOD tomorrow, bench on canary next day. if regression reproducible, we'll pair on tuning.
sam: ping me when prefetch probe ready; want to run warmup vs baseline.
aj: great. small note — watch for sawtooth behavior if token_budget oscillates; add hysteresis.
maria: good call. we'll cap adjustments to +-25% per minute.
cheng: ok. logging plan: add compat_entropy, avg_batch_size, kv_hit_rate to per-route metrics so we can correlate.
infra-bot: incident:regression created #1951239999 at 1951240090 - assigned to eng-runtime oncall
maria: thanks. I'll update thread with results and attach microbench CSVs.
